methodological_rigor.justification: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 36 studies (6,839 patients) following rigorous protocols. Comprehensive search across 10 databases (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, Web of Science, etc.) with inclusion/exclusion criteria clearly specified. Two-reviewer independent data extraction with third-reviewer dispute resolution. Quality assessment using Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS); all studies scored ≥7 (high quality). Random-effects models employed with heterogeneity assessment (I2, χ2). Sensitivity analysis and funnel plot for publication bias. Clear outcome definitions (OS, DFS, RR at multiple timepoints).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: LoE 1a (systematic review of cohort/comparative studies). Strong clinical evidence: LT superior to LR in 3-, 5-, and 10-year OS (77.4% vs 76.8%, 70.3% vs 61.6%, 57.8% vs 40.6%, respectively) and all-timepoint DFS. Lower recurrence rate with LT (absolute 17% vs ~50% with LR per background). Directly informs treatment selection for Milan criteria-eligible HCC patients. Recommendation for LT as preferred option when donor organs available has clear clinical implications.

reporting_quality.justification: PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) standards followed: systematic search strategy detailed, inclusion/exclusion criteria explicit, study selection flow diagram (PRISMA), quality assessment (Table III), data extraction methodology clear. Baseline characteristics of included studies and patient populations presented (Tables I, II, IV). Publication bias evaluation via funnel plot mentioned. Heterogeneity assessment reported for all outcomes. Supplementary data (Data S1) referenced. Some limitation: full search terms and PRISMA checklist details not explicitly provided in excerpt.

novelty_literature.justification: LT efficacy in HCC known; Milan criteria established standard. Comparison of LT vs LR previously studied. Present meta-analysis consolidates evidence and quantifies superiority of LT—confirmatory rather than novel, but provides robust synthesis of existing literature.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized with clear methods, results presented systematically (OS, then DFS, then RR) with subgroup analyses. Tables comprehensive (baseline characteristics, inclusion studies, quality scores, patient demographics, heterogeneity). Kaplan-Meier curves referenced. Discussion contextualizes findings and acknowledges organ shortage constraints. Writing is clear and appropriate for systematic review format.

key_strengths: Rigorous systematic review (36 high-quality studies, 6,839 patients) with comprehensive multi-database search and reproducible methodology.
Strong clinical evidence: LT superior in 3-year (77.4% vs 76.8% OS, P=0.01), 5-year (70.3% vs 61.6%, P<0.00001), and 10-year OS (57.8% vs 40.6%, P<0.0001).
Significantly improved DFS at all timepoints with LT (1-, 3-, 5-, 10-year) and lower recurrence rate.
High-quality included studies (all NOS ≥7); sensitivity analysis and heterogeneity assessment conducted.
key_concerns: Moderate-to-substantial heterogeneity in some analyses (I2 up to 67% for 10-year OS); sources not fully explored.
Observational studies only (retrospective cohorts); no RCTs available (acknowledged limitation of HCC treatment landscape).
Confounding variables (cirrhosis severity, MVI distribution significantly differed between groups) not adjusted in meta-analysis.
No subgroup analyses by cirrhosis class, tumor characteristics, or transplant center experience.
Transplant access/availability not modeled; recommendation may not be feasible globally.
chief_reviewer.rationale: High-quality systematic review and meta-analysis providing strong evidence that LT is superior to LR for Milan criteria-eligible HCC patients in terms of OS, DFS, and recurrence. Appropriate tier 2 publication with solid methodology and direct clinical applicability, despite retrospective data sources and residual confounding.
